what: Earlier internal measurements (October 2026) on a PRIVATE SFT dataset; reported for context, not reproducible from this repository. The public, reproducible benchmark is results/summary.json.
model: Qwen3.8-27B (hybrid: 48 Gated DeltaNet + 16 gated attention layers), block-FP8 checkpoint; baselines on the bf16 dequantisation of the same weights

workload.same_step_sets: all arms except ms-swift use the identical 300 step sets

mfu_convention: 4 x 27e9 x tokens/s/GPU / 989e12 (nameplate N, the convention used at the time)

arms.name: transformers + PEFT (bf16 base, fp32 LoRA, autocast, ckpt every layer, micro 2 x accum 4)
same + bf16 LoRA copies + chunked head, micro 4 x accum 2
ms-swift 4.5.3, padding-free + flash-attn 2 + Liger, gradient checkpointing, micro 4 x accum 2
arms.caveat: run WITH gradient checkpointing; on the public 9B benchmark swift was ~1.7x faster without it, which was not tried at 27B (72.7 GiB with checkpointing at micro 4)

arms.name: perf_kit (FP8-stored base, exact per-GEMM dequant; LPT ranks; 3,600-token packed micro-batches, 5% layers recomputed)

power: 94% of samples software-power-capped, SM clock median 1,410 MHz, ~516 W GPU draw (job 3650429)
notes: 1 GPU -> 4 GPUs cost ~3% for perf_kit at the same per-rank work (1-GPU 1.76-1.79 s/step)
